Co-directed by Lauren Montgomery, Steve Ahn, and William Mata, produced in collaboration with Nickelodeon Movies and Paramount Animation, the film was originally set to be released on October 10, 2025, before being delayed to January 30, 2026.[11][12][13] On December 23, 2025, it was announced the film would no longer receive a theatrical release and will instead premiere exclusively on Paramount+ on October 9, 2026.[8][4] Contents 1 Synopsis 2 Cast 3 Production 3.1 Development 3.2 Casting 3.3 Animation 4 Trivia 5 References 6 External links Synopsis Avatar Aang, the world's last Airbender, learns of an ancient power that could save his culture from extinction. With the help of his friends, he embarks on a global quest to find it before it falls into the wrong hands and threatens to upend the peace they sacrificed everything to achieve.[14] Cast Eric Nam - Avatar Aang[12][15] Dave Bautista - Unnamed antagonist[12][16] Jessica Matten - Katara[17] Román Zaragoza - Sokka[12][18] Dionne Quan - Toph Beifong[12][16] Steven Yeun - Zuko[19] Taika Waititi[4] Geraldine Viswanathan[4] Dee Bradley Baker[4] Peta Sergeant[4] Freida Pinto[4] Ke Huy Quan[4] Production Development On June 15, 2022, Deadline reported that three animated Avatar films were in development by Avatar Studios, with the first focusing on Avatar Aang and his friends[20][21] in their young adulthood.[22] On November 10, 2022, Variety announced that the film was scheduled for theatrical release on October 10, 2025,[23] but this date was pushed back several times, with it now due for release on October 9, 2026.[8] On December 23, 2025, it was announced that the theatrical release had been abandoned, with the film instead premiering exclusively on Paramount+.[4] On March 7, director Lauren Montgomery posted on Instagram that the film had wrapped up production.[24] Casting On November 30, 2023, Jessica Matten was confirmed to have been cast as Katara in the film via the official website of her production company, 7 Forward Entertainment.[17] On April 11, 2024, at CinemaCon, Dave Bautista, Eric Nam, Dionne Quan, and Román Zaragoza were revealed to be part of the voice cast for the film.[12] It was also confirmed that Michael Dante DiMartino, Bryan Konietzko, and Eric Coleman[12] were on board as producers alongside Latifa Ouaou and Maryann Garger.[18] It was also revealed that William Mata would be co-directing the film.[12] On April 12, 2024, Eric Nam confirmed via Instagram that he would be the voice of Aang,[15] while the official Avatar: The Last Airbender Instagram account confirmed that Dave Bautista had been cast as the villain and Dionne Quan had been cast as Toph.[16] On November 19, 2025, Jeremy Zuckerman revealed that he is scoring the film with full access to an orchestra, noting that the bigger budget for the film enables him to try new things he could not do on Avatar: The Last Airbender due to technological limits at the time.[25] Animation On October 13, 2022, it was reported that Paramount Animation and Nickelodeon Animation had enlisted Flying Bark Productions to animate the feature film. The Sydney-based studio put out a call for Australian and international artists to work on the project, which will combine traditional 2D animation with substantial CG elements.[6] On May 12, 2025, Studio Mir, the primary animation studio responsible for The Legend of Korra, announced its participation in the development of the feature film.[7] On May 16, 2025, the film's logo was revealed on social media, in addition to a new release date of October 9, 2026.[26][8] The animation style used in the feature film combines 2D hand-drawn animated characters with 3D computer-animated environments, courtesy of Deep Canvas technology.[27][28] Trivia Previous logo from when the movie was referred to as The Legend of Aang: The Last Airbender. This will be Avatar Studios' first film. The film was developed under the working title Aang: The Last Airbender and was eventually changed to The Legend of Aang: The Last Airbender, before finally landing on Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender.[29][10] Kat Tsai, a crew member on the film's production, likened its blending of 2D and 3D animation to Disney's Tarzan, where hand-drawn characters were supplemented with computer-generated background elements.[30] The film will have at least four books based on its release.
